title: The volcano in Peru that starved Russia 🌋
subject: volcano
description:
Could one eruption do this again today? 👇

In February 1600, Huaynaputina in Peru produced the largest eruption ever recorded in South America. Tree rings show 1601 brought the Northern Hemisphere's worst short-term cooling in 600 years, and Russia fell into its deadliest famine.

Sources: Briffa et al. 1998, Nature 393:450-455; Verosub & Lippman 2008, Eos (AGU) 89(15), via UC Davis ("1600 Eruption Caused Global Disruption"); Wikipedia: Huaynaputina, Russian famine of 1601-1603

scenes.text: A volcano in Peru starved Russia.
On 19 February 1600, Huaynaputina exploded. No eruption recorded in South America has been bigger.
Its sulfur haze circled the planet, and 1601 brought the sharpest Northern Hemisphere cooling in 600 years.
In Russia, the harvests failed in 1601 and 1602. Moscow alone buried 127,000 people in mass graves.
About 2 million died, nearly a third of the country.
Geologist Ken Verosub, who tied the famine to the eruption, admits he can't prove the volcano caused it all.
